name: Open Rummy
description: Open Rummy is an Indian partnership rummy game popular in Rajasthan and among Marwari families. Played with 3-4 standard decks plus printed jokers and sliding jokers (Twos). Players draw from an open discard pile (like 500 Rummy); only Aces and Threes can form equal-card groups. First team to 1,500 points wins.
deck: 3-4 standard 52-card decks plus 3 printed jokers per deck (220 cards for 4-player standard)

history.origins: Open Rummy is popular in Rajasthan, especially Jhunjhunu District among Marwari families. The open discard pile from which multiple cards can be drawn is reminiscent of 500 Rummy, which was sometimes known in America as 'Pinochle Rummy'.
timeline: Developed in Rajasthan and Marwari communities.
Present: A game of strategy and intellect that can keep players busy for hours.
history.cultural: A staple of Marwari social and family play, often played for long sessions.
history.evolution: Unique restrictions: only Aces and Threes form equal-card groups; sequences require at least one natural card and at most three jokers. Bonuses for complete sets (12 cards 3-A in a suit) and suited groups of Threes or Aces.

setup.players: 4 or 6 players in two teams; partners sit alternately (each player between two opponents). No peeking at partner's cards or communication.
setup.deck: 3 or 4 standard decks plus printed jokers (peeniya/khabuchiya); all Twos are sliding jokers (duggi). Cards rank 3-A.
setup.dealing: First dealer chosen randomly; deal rotates left. Dealer shuffles, opponent to dealer's right cuts. 45 cards each (4-player, 4-deck); 40 remain as closed pile. Top card turned face-up to start discard pile.

rules.objective: First team to reach 1,500 points (4-deck standard). Score from cards on table, opponent unplayed cards, complete-set bonuses, suited-group bonuses, and show bonus.
rules.gameplay: 1. Turn order: discard (compulsory) â†’ play combinations (optional) â†’ draw (compulsory). 2. Draw: one from closed pile OR any number from discard pile (if at least one drawn card is immediately played). 3. Combinations: sequences (3+ consecutive same suit; max 3 jokers, min 1 natural); groups of 3+ Threes or 3+ Aces (no jokers). 4. Printed jokers can be replaced by natural cards and reused; sliding jokers (Twos) stay in sequence when replaced, slid to one end. 5. To declare show: team must have 5+ complete sets, at least one pure (no jokers). Wrong show = 0 for declaring team. 6. Ground show: when draw pile empties, player may declare or draw from discard and play one turn.
keyRules: Only Aces and Threes form equal-card groups.
Sequences: max 3 jokers, min 1 natural per sequence.
Taking from discard: must play at least one drawn card immediately.
Show requires 5 complete sets (12 cards 3-A per suit), 1 pure.
Partners cannot share meld area; each player has own area.

strategy.basic: Build sequences in suits where you have natural cards. Use sliding jokers at sequence ends for flexibility.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate with partner via play (no verbal communication). Avoid opening sequences in same suit as partner if you might need them for a complete set. Track discard pile depthâ€”taking multiple cards requires playing at least one.
strategy.advanced: Complete pure sets earn highest bonus (20 pts). Suited groups of 4 Aces or 4 Threes (laid together) score 75. Plan show requirements: 5 complete sets, 1 pure. Don't wrong-show.
tips: Sequences cannot be split or rearranged. Plan overlaps carefully.
Discarding a joker turns the whole discard pile face-down and removes it from play.

scoring.description: Cumulative team score. Card values: 3-6=0.5, 7-K=1, A=1.5, 2=2, joker=4. Bonuses for complete sets, suited groups. Show bonus 20.
scoring.winCondition: First team to 1,500 points. Tie if both exceed in same show.
